feature: HTTP/2 WebTransport server admission, receiver capacity and pending cleanup

behavior.command_budget: shared queue admission uses the original deadline and cancellation checks before commit; the server owner validates command expiration before Session or request lookup
behavior.request_waiters: max_request_waiters defaults to 64 and reserves one unit from receiveRequest queue commit through completion, separately from normal command queue capacity; full request-receiver budget returns RequestWaiterCapacity
behavior.reservation_release: complete, expired, canceled and shutdown request receivers release their reservation; admission prunes expired or abandoned linked waiters, and canceled receivers trigger an immediate owner deadline
behavior.pending_cleanup: PendingRequest drop publishes a generation-scoped cleanup marker in the fixed pending table without Job allocation, mutex acquisition or command capacity; owner drains after claim and before execution
behavior.wake: the sole owner clears its event with acquire/release RMW, then rechecks cleanup/cancellation predicates; this consumes prior release publications instead of clearing a wake while missing its associated state
behavior.structure: queue, generation marker and wake helpers live in endpoint/; server waiter and cleanup policies remain in endpoint_server/

regressions: 19 public server deadline entry points under held queue mutex return Timeout or Canceled without queue, receiver, Session or stream-ID changes; expired and wrong-clock calls do not enter lock wait
one waiting request receiver exhausts max_request_waiters=1 while Session commands still execute with max_queued_commands=1; cancellation and expiry restore request-receiver capacity
an expired linked receiver reservation is reclaimed during new admission, and expired queued acceptance is rejected before pending-handle lookup
pending metadata drop under a held mutex and full queue does not allocate or wait; owner cleans the pending slot before queued work executes
retained PendingRequest metadata remains safe to release after endpoint owner destruction
the authenticated TLS server test denies dropping-caller allocation while discarding a genuine pending CONNECT and requires a queued cleanup marker with unchanged queue capacity

independent Python client requires CANCEL before accepting any response for a dropped pending CONNECT, then opens a new Session on the same connection; native EndpointServer requires the same pending slot with a new generation and exact DATAGRAM/CLOSE delivery
verification.allocation_fault_boundary: denied allocation is restricted to the dropping caller; the capture proves allocation-free cleanup publication and subsequent owner cleanup, not arbitrary failures during later protocol output

remaining_scope: server owner initialization/teardown budgets, broader protocol integration and long-duration/high-concurrency evidence remain open for the overall goal
